questions.text: What is the unit digit of (7^95 × 3^57)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Unit digit cycles – 7⁴=1, 95 mod 4 = 3 → 7³ ends with 3. 3⁴=1, 57 mod 4 = 1 → 3¹ ends with 3. 3 × 3 = 9. Full solution: 7^95 → cycle (7,9,3,1) position 3 → 3. 3^57 → cycle (3,9,7,1) position 1 → 3. Product unit digit = 3×3 = 9.

questions.text: The present age of A is 1.5 times that of B. Four years ago, A's age was twice B's age. What is the present age of A?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Let B's age = x, then A = 1.5x. Four years ago: 1.5x – 4 = 2(x – 4) → 0.5x = 4 → x = 8 → A = 12 years. Full solution: Set up equations A = 1.5B and A–4 = 2(B–4). Substitute A = 1.5B → 1.5B – 4 = 2B – 8 → 0.5B = 4 → B = 8, A = 12.

questions.text: A person walks 10 m north, then turns right and walks 15 m, then turns left and walks 10 m, then turns left and walks 15 m. What is the straight-line distance from the starting point?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The path traces a rectangle; the final position is directly north of the start by the sum of the two northward legs (10 m + 10 m = 20 m). Step‑by‑step: Start (0,0). North 10 → (0,10). Right (east) 15 → (15,10). Left (north) 10 → (15,20). Left (west) 15 → (0,20). Distance = 20 m.

questions.text: In a certain code language, each letter is replaced by its mirror image in the alphabet (A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X, …). What will be the code for the word "MANGO"?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the Atbash cipher – each letter maps to its mirror (A↔Z, B↔Y, …). For MANGO: M(13)→N(14), A(1)→Z(26), N(14)→M(13), G(7)→T(20), O(15)→L(12) → NZMTL. Full solution: Write alphabet positions 1‑26. Mirror position = 27 − original position. Compute each letter's mirror and convert back to letter. M=13 → 14=N; A=1 → 26=Z; N=14 → 13=M; G=7 → 20=T; O=15 → 12=L. Hence the code is NZMTL.

questions.text: A sum of money becomes ₹1,331 in 3 years at 10% per annum compound interest compounded annually. What was the principal?
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. **To burn the midnight oil**

options.label: B
options.text: To work late into the night

questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate literal meanings (Options A, C, D). 'Midnight oil' refers to lamp oil used for light before electricity; burning it at midnight implies working/studying late. Full Solution: The idiom originates from the time when oil lamps were used for lighting at night. 'Burning the midnight oil' literally meant staying up late using lamp oil to work or study. Thus, it figuratively means to work late into the night.

questions.text: Read the sentence to find out whether there is any grammatical error in it. The error, if any, will be in one part of the sentence. The letter of that part is the answer. If there is no error, the answer is 'D'. (Ignore punctuation errors, if any.) **He has been working (A) / here for (B) / five years (C) / No error (D)**
questions.solution: Shortcut: Check 'since' vs 'for' rule. 'Since' denotes a point of time (e.g., since 2020); 'for' denotes a period/duration (e.g., for 5 years). The sentence uses 'for five years' (duration), which is correct. Present Perfect Continuous 'has been working' is correctly used for an action started in past and continuing. Full Solution: Part A uses correct tense (Present Perfect Continuous). Part B correctly uses preposition 'for' with a duration of time ('five years'). Part C is grammatically sound. The sentence is entirely correct; hence, the answer is 'No error'.

questions.text: In the following alphabet series, what will come in place of the question mark? A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The gaps between consecutive letters increase by 1 each time (+2, +3, +4, +5, +6). So the next gap is +6; O (15th) +6 = 21st = U. Step‑by‑step: A→C (+2), C→F (+3), F→J (+4), J→O (+5), therefore O→? = +6 → U.

questions.text: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use option elimination — the oath is administered by the head of the judiciary (CJI), not the executive (PM, VP) or legal advisor (AG). Step-by-step: Article 60 of the Constitution mandates that the President's oath be administered by the Chief Justice of India, or in their absence, the senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court available.

questions.text: Which blood group is designated as the 'Universal Donor' for packed red blood cell transfusions in emergency situations?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Remember 'O Negative' lacks A, B, and Rh antigens (universal donor); 'AB Positive' has all (universal recipient). Eliminate AB+ (recipient), A- (has A antigen), B+ (has B & Rh antigens). Step-by-step: O Negative red cells possess no A, B, or Rh(D) antigens on their surface, minimizing the risk of hemolytic transfusion reactions when the recipient's blood type is unknown.

questions.text: Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Take LCM of 12, 15, 20 = 60 units (tank capacity). Pipe A fills 5 units/hr, B fills 4 units/hr, C empties 3 units/hr. Net fill = 6 units/hr → time = 60/6 = 10 hrs. Full solution: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/15 – 1/20 = (5+4–3)/60 = 6/60 = 1/10 tank per hour, so 10 hours to fill.

questions.text: Choose the word that best substitutes the given group of words. **A person who hates mankind**
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use root words. 'Miso-' means hatred (misogyny), 'anthro-' means mankind (anthropology). 'Phil-' means love (philanthropist), 'biblio-' means books (bibliophile), 'ascetic' denotes self-discipline. Full Solution: 'Misanthrope' is derived from Greek 'misos' (hatred) and 'anthropos' (mankind). A philanthropist loves mankind, a bibliophile loves books, and an ascetic practices severe self-discipline. Therefore, 'Misanthrope' is the correct one-word substitution.

questions.text: Which river is popularly known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent devastating floods and frequent course changes?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Associate 'Sorrow' with high silt load and avulsion (course shifting); Kosi is infamous for shifting over 100km westward. Eliminate Ganga (main trunk), Gandak (relatively stable), Mahananda (smaller tributary). Step-by-step: The Kosi River carries massive sediment from the Himalayas, raising its bed level and causing frequent breaches of embankments, leading to catastrophic floods in North Bihar.

questions.text: Who was the first Indian woman to serve as the President of the United Nations General Assembly?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use role elimination. Sarojini Naidu was a poet/governor; Indira Gandhi was PM; Sucheta Kripalani was first woman CM of a state (UP). The diplomatic role of UNGA President fits Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit, a career diplomat and sister of Nehru. Full Solution: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit was elected President of the 8th session of the UN General Assembly in 1953, becoming the first woman and first Indian to hold the post. Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of an Indian state (UP). Indira Gandhi was the first woman Prime Minister of India. Sucheta Kripalani was the first woman Chief Minister of an Indian state (UP).

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'TABLE' is written as 'UBCMF'. How will 'CHAIR' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Every letter is shifted forward by one position in the alphabet (T→U, A→B, B→C, L→M, E→F). Apply the same +1 shift to CHAIR: C→D, H→I, A→B, I→J, R→S → DIBJS. Step‑by‑step: Verify the given code follows a uniform +1 shift, then replicate for the target word.
